meta.title: Interview Question Bank — Founding Product Designer
meta.company: Stealth · Thejo venture studio · AI-native tool for product teams · Fully remote

categories.name: Recruiter / phone screen
categories.probing_for: Basic fit, motivation, comp alignment, communication, no red flags. Low on craft, high on signal.
categories.your_angle: Calm, selective, specific. You're choosing, not escaping. Land the Flash→AI design-engineering throughline in 30 seconds.

categories.name: Behavioral & career narrative
categories.probing_for: Self-awareness, growth, how you handle conflict and failure. STAR structure expected.
categories.your_angle: 25 years = range and pattern-recognition, not staleness. Pick stories that show you still ship and still retool. Lead with specificity and a real outcome, including the not-so-happy endings.

categories.name: Motivation & fit
categories.probing_for: Whether you'll actually leave, whether you'll stay, whether the mission lands.
categories.your_angle: You've used your own client's "we can't do remote/comp" as the honest reason — forward-looking, no Pfizer baggage. The product *is* your wheelhouse, so conviction is genuine.

categories.name: Design process & craft
categories.probing_for: How you actually think, not the textbook. They've heard "research → ideate → prototype → test" four thousand times. Specificity and opinions win.
categories.your_angle: Show a process that flexes for speed, and where AI and code now sit inside it. Have opinions.

categories.name: Portfolio deep-dive
categories.probing_for: Real ownership, business context, tradeoffs, measurable impact, storytelling. Target ~18–22 min per case, leave room for questions.
categories.your_angle: Lead each case with the strategic bet, your specific role, the problem framing, iterations (not just final mocks), what you cut/pushed back on, cross-functional collaboration, and quantified outcome. Bring the hardships, not just the wins.
notes: Your strongest cases to have loaded: AI-ready design system overhaul (~60 components, Shadcn vs. in-house decision) · Figma plugin (multi-day → two clicks) · VOX / Cursor / Claude Code builds · HemaSense · North Face wear-tester tool.

categories.name: Live design critique / teardown
categories.probing_for: Articulation, taste, structured thinking on your feet, ability to be specific and kind.
categories.your_angle: Use a repeatable critique frame (user goal → flow → hierarchy → interaction → edge cases → systemization). Voice the *why*, propose alternatives, welcome questions like a tech lead.

categories.name: Product sense & strategy
categories.probing_for: Business thinking, prioritization, metrics literacy — graded as heavily as craft at senior level.
categories.your_angle: You are both the *user* and a *builder* of tooling for product teams. Frame answers around time-to-value, leverage, and the design-velocity problem you've lived.

categories.name: Design systems
categories.probing_for: Depth here, because it's your specialty and central to the role. Expect them to go deep.
categories.your_angle: This is home turf. Talk tokens, governance, adoption, and — your differentiator — building systems that are *consumable by AI coding tools*.

categories.name: Design engineering & the design–code boundary
categories.probing_for: Whether your "design engineer" claim is real. They may probe technically or ask you to show code/prototypes.
categories.your_angle: Your edge and the Flash→ActionScript→AI throughline. Be concrete about what you build, ship, and prototype in code. Don't overclaim full SWE; claim fluent design-engineering.

categories.name: AI-native design
categories.probing_for: Now a must-answer category. Both how you *use* AI in your workflow and how you *design* AI products. Show AI augments your creativity, not replaces it.
categories.your_angle: You're ahead of the curve here — you've built AI-augmented workflows and AI-ready systems. Also be ready for the ethics/trust dimension.

categories.name: Collaboration & cross-functional
categories.probing_for: Whether you make teams better, especially with eng and founders at close range.
categories.your_angle: Your code fluency makes you an unusually low-friction partner for engineers. Show concrete rituals (critique, design QA, pairing).

categories.name: Staff+ scope & leadership
categories.probing_for: That you operate at staff level — judgment, influence, multiplying others — even as an IC.
categories.your_angle: You've managed people and run craft; here you're a "super IC" who sets the bar and the system without needing a big org.

categories.name: Startup readiness
categories.probing_for: The quiet concern — can an enterprise-pharma contractor handle startup pace and ambiguity?
categories.your_angle: Counter with your scrappy solo building: career-ops CLI, plugins, Cursor/Claude Code experiments, Obsidian knowledge system. You ship fast and alone.

categories.name: Founder round — Thejo / Shawn
categories.probing_for: Conviction, vision-fit, intellectual partnership, whether they'd want to build alongside you. Good candidates ask deep questions back.
categories.your_angle: Meet them as a peer. Shawn = craft bar (Discord/Airbase); Thejo = builder who's done it twice. Show taste, opinions, and genuine curiosity about the bet.

categories.name: Curveballs & weakness probes
categories.probing_for: Composure and self-awareness on the things they're privately unsure about.
categories.your_angle: Name the concern before they fully press it, then reframe. Don't get defensive.

categories.name: Take-home / design exercise prompts
categories.probing_for: End-to-end thinking under realistic constraints. Senior loops often use a 0-to-1 brief with business constraints; sometimes a "design jam" or a build-it prototype given your code fluency.
categories.your_angle: Show the thinking, not just final mocks. Document the bet, the cuts, the tradeoffs. If you can, prototype in code to demonstrate the design-eng edge.

categories.name: Questions to ask THEM
categories.probing_for: (yours) Real fit, and signaling seniority. Good questions are half the interview.
categories.your_angle: Tailor by who you're talking to. Probe the design-eng scope, the stage, and the team.

questions.text: Tell me about yourself / walk me through your background.
Why are you open to something new right now?
What are you looking for in your next role?
What caught your eye about this company / this role?
What do you know about us so far?
What's your current situation — are you employed, contracting, how soon could you start?
Are you interviewing elsewhere? Where are you in those processes?
This is fully remote — does that work for you long-term?
What are your compensation expectations? (see comp prep sheet — flip it)
What's your timeline for making a decision?
Any questions for me before we go further?
Tell me about a project that didn't go as planned. What did you learn?
Tell me about a time you killed your own design or reversed a strong opinion.
Tell me about the hardest design problem you've solved.
Describe a time you received tough feedback. What did you do with it?
Tell me about a disagreement with a PM or engineer and how it resolved.
Tell me about a time you had to influence without authority.
Walk me through a project you're most proud of — and one you'd redo.
Tell me about a time you had to make a decision with incomplete information.
How do you handle a stakeholder who overrides your design judgment?
Describe a time you mentored someone or leveled up a team.
What's a professional risk you took that didn't pay off?
How do you stay current? What have you learned recently? (← lean into AI retooling)
Why leave a stable contract for an early-stage startup?
Why this company specifically, out of everything you could do?
What excites you about an AI-native tool for helping product teams build faster?
Why a founding / early-stage role at this point in your career?
What would make this the right next move for the next 3–5 years?
What kind of work makes you lose track of time?
What are you optimizing for right now — money, equity, craft, autonomy, mission?
What would make you turn this down?
How do you feel about the ambiguity of pre-product-market-fit work?
What do you know about Shawn's and Thejo's work, and does it resonate?
Walk me through your end-to-end design process.
How does that process change at startup speed vs. a large org?
How do you go from a vague problem to a shipped solution?
How do you decide when something is "good enough" to ship?
How do you balance craft / polish against velocity?
How do you incorporate user research when there's little time or data?
What does "quality" mean to you in product design?
How do you know when a design is right? What signals do you trust?
What's your relationship with prototyping — lo-fi, hi-fi, code?
How do you handle the jump from one big idea to many edge cases (0→1 to 1→n)?
What's a design principle you hold that others might disagree with?
How do you keep taste and consistency across a fast-moving product?
Walk me through your strongest case study, end to end.
What was your specific role — solo, lead, or contributor?
How did you define the problem? What was the strategic bet?
What were the key tradeoffs, and what did you push back on or cut?
What was the measurable impact? Did you revisit the metrics after launch?
Show me a project where the outcome fell short. What happened?
What would you have done with more time or budget?
To what extent do you "own" this work? Who else touched it?
Why did you make this specific decision over the alternatives?
How did you collaborate with engineering and PM on this?
Tell me about the Shadcn vs. in-house decision — how did you reason about it?
Walk me through the Figma plugin — what problem, what impact, how did you build it?
Do you have a side project or experiment you'd want to talk about?
Here's a screen / flow from our product — critique it.
Redesign this screen for maximum activation. (interviewer shows a screen)
What's wrong with this onboarding flow, and how would you fix it?
Pick an app you use daily and tell us what you'd change.
What's a product with great design? What makes it great?
What's a recent design decision (anywhere) you strongly disagree with?
Critique our marketing site / our competitor's product.
How would you improve [their product's] core loop?
Design a tool that helps product teams build 10x faster — how would you start? (almost certain)
How would you measure whether a design change actually worked?
How would you prioritize what to build first with limited resources?
Design a 0-to-1 productivity tool for small teams.
What's broken about how product teams build today?
How do you decide what *not* to build?
What metrics would you own as the founding designer here?
How would you think about the first 90 days of the product / your areas?
How do you balance a single power user's needs against the broad base?
What would a "10x faster" workflow actually feel like to a user?
How would you define success for the design function in year one?
Tell me about a time you influenced product strategy as a designer.
Walk me through how you'd scope a design system from scratch here.
How do you make a design system consumable by AI tools (Cursor, Copilot, v0)?
How do you balance consistency (the system) with innovation (new patterns)?
How do you structure tokens (color, type, spacing, motion)?
How do you keep design and code in sync?
How do you drive adoption of a design system across a team?
When do you build in-house vs. adopt something like Shadcn? How do you decide?
How do you document components so both humans and AI can use them?
How do you handle versioning and breaking changes in a living system?
What's the right *amount* of system for an early-stage company?
How do you measure the health or ROI of a design system?
How do you handle a designer who wants to break the system?
How comfortable are you working in code? Where's the line for you?
How do you decide when to prototype in code vs. in Figma?
Tell me about something you built that lived in the browser / in production.
How do you collaborate with engineers — at the spec, the PR, or both?
What's your stack? (Figma Make, Cursor, Claude Code, React/Vite/Tailwind…)
How do you think about the handoff problem? Is handoff even the right model?
Walk me through a tool or plugin you built to speed up a workflow.
How do you keep prototypes from becoming throwaway?
Where does design engineering add the most leverage at an early-stage startup?
How much of this role do you *want* to be at the code edge vs. pure IC design? (← your fit question, asked back at you)
How do you use AI in your design workflow today? Be specific.
How would you design for an AI feature that's wrong ~5% of the time?
How do you design trust, transparency, and user control into AI products?
Where does AI help in design, and where does it actively hurt?
How do you keep craft and taste when AI accelerates output?
How do you think about bias and inclusivity in AI-driven experiences?
What's the role of the designer when AI can generate UI?
How would you design the "human in the loop" moments in an AI tool?
What AI design pattern do you think is overused or broken right now?
How do you see the product designer's job changing over the next 2–3 years?
How do you work with engineers day to day?
How do you partner with a PM (or a founder acting as PM)?
How do you handle competing priorities across stakeholders?
How do you give and receive design critique?
Tell me about a cross-functional conflict you navigated well.
How do you communicate design decisions to non-designers?
How do you keep alignment without slowing everyone down?
How do you handle being the only / most senior designer in the room?
What does operating at a staff/founding level mean to you here?
How would you set up the design function and rituals from scratch?
How do you raise the craft bar across a team without managing them?
How do you decide where to spend your own time as the senior designer?
How do you mentor or grow other designers?
How do you turn a recurring problem into a process or system improvement?
How would you tie design work to business outcomes / OKRs?
When would you want to hire the next designer, and what would you look for?
How do you earn design a seat at the table with leadership?
How do you handle ambiguity with no PM, no research team, no roadmap?
Tell me about a time you wore many hats / did work outside your role.
How do you move fast without sacrificing the things that matter?
What's your reaction when priorities change weekly?
How do you self-direct when no one is assigning you work?
What have you built recently with little or no support?
How do you handle the emotional reality of pre-PMF uncertainty?
Coming from regulated enterprise work, how will you adjust to startup chaos? (address head-on)
Why do *you* think product teams are slow today, and what would actually fix it?
What's your vision for how design and AI reshape how software gets built?
What would you want to be true about this product in 12 months?
What kind of designer do you want to become here?
What's a strong, maybe contrarian, opinion you hold about design or AI?
How do you think about risk — for the product and for your own career?
What would make you say this venture is succeeding? Failing?
Tell me about the last hypothesis you killed and what you learned.
What do you need from a founder to do your best work?
You have 25 years of experience — are you too senior / too expensive for a founding IC role? (reframe: adaptability, retooling around AI now)
Most of your recent work is enterprise/regulated — can you do scrappy 0-to-1? (reframe: your solo builds)
What's your biggest weakness as a designer?
Where are you weakest technically, and how do you compensate?
What kind of work do you *not* want to do?
Why haven't you done a startup before now?
How do we know you'll still be hungry and hands-on, not just directing?
What would your last team say is frustrating about working with you?
If we hire you and it's not working in 6 months, what likely went wrong?
Design a 0-to-1 feature for [their product space] given these constraints.
Improve a core flow in our product and justify your choices.
Design an onboarding experience for an AI-native tool.
Take a messy real workflow and design a 10x-faster version.
Scope a minimal design system for a brand-new product.
Build a working prototype of [small feature] (code or Figma Make).
Present a past project as a structured 20-minute deep dive.
What stage and funding is the company at?
What does the interview process look like end to end?
What range is budgeted for this level?
How much of this role lives at the design-engineering edge vs. pure IC design?
What are the 1–2 core areas you'd want this person to own?
How do you and the team think about craft vs. speed right now?
What does the design function look like today, and where is it going?
What's the hardest design problem the product faces right now?
What's the core bet, and what has to be true for it to win?
What have you learned so far that surprised you?
How do you want design to influence product direction, not just execution?
What's the runway and the next big milestone?
What would success in this role look like at 3, 6, and 12 months?
What's it like to work here on a hard day?
Why is this role open / why now?
What's the biggest risk to the company you'd want me to know going in?
Are you considering other roles, and how does this compare?
What's your timeline and decision criteria?
What would it take for you to say yes?
When could you start? Any notice or wind-down on your current contract?
Compensation expectations / reaction to the range. (→ comp prep sheet)
Anything that would stop you from accepting an offer?
